_about: The single source of truth for every mechanic term. Fantasy first, rule second. docs/vocabulary.md is generated from this file by tools/export_vocabulary.gd. status: implemented (in sim/), planned (designed, not coded), idea (floated, undecided).

entries.name: Hull
entries.fantasy: The machine itself. When it is gone, the machine is a wreck.
entries.rule: Damage that gets past shield removes hull. Hull never recovers during a battle. At zero the mech is a wreck to be salvaged after the battle.

entries.name: Shield
entries.fantasy: A buffer that buys you a few rounds to solve the squad before it starts costing you the machine.
entries.rule: Enemy damage removes shield before hull. Shield faces add shield up to the chassis maximum. Shields recharge fully between skirmishes.
entries.holes: Option not coded: recharge only during phases spent out of combat.

entries.name: Heat
entries.fantasy: Every gun has a price, and the big ones are paid in smoke.
entries.rule: Attack faces may add heat. Heat above the chassis maximum spills into hull damage one for one. Vent faces remove heat.
entries.holes: Heat does nothing below the cap. Consider effects at high heat short of overflow.

entries.name: Reroll
entries.fantasy: You do not like what you see. You get two chances to change your mind.
entries.rule: Two rerolls per round, each rerolling every unlocked, unspent mech die. Rerolls may be spent before or after attacking, so a low damage roll is information for the rest of the round. Never pooled across rounds.

entries.name: Rift Pressure
entries.fantasy: The city is running out of time, and there is a bar on screen that says so.
entries.rule: Ticks once per battlefield phase and once per skirmish round. When full it resets and a fresh squad emerges at the rift.
entries.holes: Spawns a fixed squad. Should draw from the battle's faction and escalate.

entries.name: Gate Integrity
entries.fantasy: The last wall of mankind. If it falls the campaign is over.
entries.rule: A squad whose path reaches the gate strikes it instead of moving. Gate integrity persists across battles and is repaired in the meta.
entries.holes: Gate damage formula is a placeholder (strength divided by three).

entries.name: Attack face
entries.fantasy: A gun, a claw, a shell. The primary icon is its reach.
entries.rule: Spend on a foe within reach to deal its power in damage, then apply its keywords and heat.

entries.name: Shield face
entries.fantasy: Raise the plating. Yours or a friend's.
entries.rule: Spend on self or an ally to add its power in shield, capped at that mech's shield maximum.

entries.name: Vent face
entries.fantasy: Blow the heat out of the reactor before it blows out of the hull.
entries.rule: Spend on self or an ally to remove its power in heat.

entries.name: Cracked face
entries.fantasy: Something inside is broken and the die shows it.
entries.rule: Does nothing when rolled. Only a destroyed face is blank; a cracked face still acts. Persists until repaired in the hangar.

entries.name: Damage range
entries.fantasy: Kinetic weapons do not promise. They roll.
entries.rule: A kinetic attack face shows a minimum and a maximum and rolls between them when spent, immediately and visibly. Energy faces show one number and never roll. Numbers are in tens.
entries.holes: Ranges are content-authored per component; no upgrade path raises min or max yet.

entries.name: Critical hit
entries.fantasy: Sometimes the round finds the seam.
entries.rule: A kinetic face may carry a crit chance. On a crit the roll is doubled before other multipliers. Energy faces never crit. Crits fire the on_crit passive trigger.
entries.holes: No crit-chance upgrades yet; no visible crit chance on the die face beyond the description.

entries.name: Line of fire
entries.fantasy: If you can see it, you can shoot it. If something is in the way, shoot that first.
entries.rule: Targets any front-rank foe, and any back-rank foe whose column is exposed.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.fantasy: Over the wall and onto the thing behind it. Just do not aim it at your own feet.
entries.rule: Targets any foe in either rank. Hitting the front rank triggers danger close.

entries.name: Cleave
entries.fantasy: One swing, three ghouls.
entries.rule: Also hits the foes in the neighbouring columns of the target's rank.

entries.name: Pierce
entries.fantasy: The railgun does not care who is standing in front of whom.
entries.rule: Also hits the foe in the other rank of the target's column.

entries.name: Burn
entries.fantasy: Set it alight and let it think about its choices.
entries.rule: Adds one burn stack per 20 damage dealt, rounded up. Each round the foe takes 10 per stack, then loses one stack.

entries.name: Suppress
entries.fantasy: The big hit it was winding up never lands.
entries.rule: The target skips its telegraphed action this round.

entries.name: Overcharge
entries.fantasy: Push the reactor past the red line and hope the housing holds.
entries.rule: Double the face's damage and double its heat.

entries.name: Execute
entries.fantasy: Finish it before it gets back up.
entries.rule: Double damage against a foe at or below half its health.

entries.name: Chain
entries.fantasy: The arc jumps to whoever looks weakest.
entries.rule: Also hits the lowest-health foe within reach other than the target.

entries.name: Lock
entries.fantasy: That roll was too good to let go.
entries.rule: After this face is spent, the die keeps it into next round instead of rolling.

entries.name: Steady
entries.fantasy: No surprises. That is the whole point of it.
entries.rule: A ranged face with steady always deals its average instead of rolling. It may still crit.

entries.name: Flip
entries.fantasy: Turn the die over. The other side is usually better.
entries.rule: Set another mech's die to the face opposite its current one.
entries.holes: Needs a definition of opposite faces for non-d6 dice.

entries.name: Copy
entries.fantasy: Whatever they rolled, you rolled too.
entries.rule: Set this die to the current face of an ally's die.

entries.name: Reflect
entries.fantasy: Hit me. See what happens.
entries.rule: While shield from this face remains, foes that strike this mech take damage equal to the face's power.
entries.holes: Would need shield sources to be tracked separately.

entries.name: Burning
entries.fantasy: On fire, and getting less on fire every round.
entries.rule: Foe status. See the burn keyword.

entries.name: Suppressed
entries.fantasy: Head down, gun silent.
entries.rule: Foe status. Skips its action this round, then clears.

entries.name: Cracked face
entries.fantasy: They got through the armour and something important is bent.
entries.rule: Mech status, global rule. When a hit gets past shield and takes at least a quarter of maximum hull in one blow, there is a one-in-two chance one intact face cracks: it loses its keywords, crit chance and unique effect, but still does its basic action. Counterplay is shield before a big telegraphed hit. A cracked face is a damaged component: it persists across skirmishes and battles until repaired in the hangar.
entries.holes: Threshold and chance are placeholders. Repair cost and the hangar screen are not built.

entries.name: Destroyed face
entries.fantasy: Hit where it was already broken.
entries.rule: Mech status. When an injury lands on a face that is already cracked, the component is destroyed: the face is blank and does nothing when rolled, until the hangar repairs or replaces it.

entries.name: Locked
entries.fantasy: Held for next round.
entries.rule: Die status. See the lock keyword.

entries.name: Front rank
entries.fantasy: The bodies.
entries.rule: Three slots. Front-preferring foes fill these first. Always in line of fire.

entries.name: Back rank
entries.fantasy: The problems.
entries.rule: Three slots behind the front. Back-preferring foes hold these and never step up. Front-preferring foes wait here and step up when the slot ahead empties.

entries.name: Exposed
entries.fantasy: Kill the ghoul and the necromancer behind it is suddenly very interested in cover.
entries.rule: A back-rank foe is exposed when the front slot in its column is empty. Exposed foes are in line of fire.

entries.name: Squad pool
entries.fantasy: There are always more where those came from.
entries.rule: Foes not yet on the field. Empty slots refill from the pool after each round. The skirmish is won when the field and the pool are both empty.
entries.holes: Elites should surface at set points rather than in pool order.

entries.name: Step up
entries.fantasy: The horde closes the gap.
entries.rule: After the dead are cleared, a front-preferring foe in the back rank moves into an empty front slot in its column.

entries.name: Danger close
entries.fantasy: You mortared the thing in your face. Your shields are now also in your face.
entries.rule: Indirect fire on the front rank removes shield from the firing mech equal to half the face's power, rounded up.

entries.name: Massive
entries.fantasy: Too big for one slot. Too big for one anything.
entries.rule: A massive foe fills both slots of a column and counts as front rank. Its column is never exposed while it stands. Only some elites and bosses are massive.
entries.holes: Cleave treats it as a front-rank neighbour; pierce cannot hit anything behind it because nothing is.

entries.name: Withdraw
entries.fantasy: Enough. Fall back and let the map decide the rest.
entries.rule: Available at the start of any round after the first, before any face is spent, so there is never free damage. Ends the skirmish; survivors on both sides carry their damage to the battlefield.

entries.name: Movespeed
entries.fantasy: How much ground it covers before the enemy moves.
entries.rule: Movement points per phase. Entering a hex costs its terrain's move cost for that unit's traits.

entries.name: Intent
entries.fantasy: You can see where they are going. Whether they get there is up to you.
entries.rule: Each squad's path for the phase is previewed exactly. It heads for the gate or the nearest city defense, or hunts mechs if aggro. Player routes resolve first.
entries.holes: Aggro is a fixed flag. Should be a behaviour per foe type.

entries.name: Body block
entries.fantasy: Stand in the road. They stop.
entries.rule: A squad stops at the first hex on its path occupied by a blocking unit. Flyers do not block; squads pass through their hex but never land on it.

entries.name: Contact
entries.fantasy: Adjacent means fighting.
entries.rule: After all movement, every connected group of adjacent units that contains both sides becomes one skirmish. Multiple skirmishes resolve one at a time.
entries.holes: No participant cap. May need one for phone readability.

entries.name: Squad
entries.fantasy: One hex, one kind of thing, several of them.
entries.rule: An enemy hex is a squad: one foe type times a strength. A skirmish's enemy composition is whatever squads are chained together at contact, so the rift's formation and the player's disruption of it decide what you fight. Bosses are single three-hex units.

entries.name: Footprint
entries.fantasy: Some things do not fit in a hex.
entries.rule: A unit covers one or more hexes. A boss covers three in a triangle. Every footprint hex blocks, touches for contact, and is a tap target. Squads and mechs stay single-hex.
entries.holes: Footprints do not rotate with facing.

entries.name: Structure
entries.fantasy: The gate is not a hex. It is a wall.
entries.rule: Gate and rift hexes are structures wider than one hex. Nobody stands on them. A squad whose path reaches any gate hex strikes the gate.
entries.holes: The rift does nothing yet beyond marking where squads spawn.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.fantasy: The rift coughs up another squad.
entries.rule: When Rift Pressure fills, the next squad of the faction's spawn list appears on the nearest free hex to the rift.
entries.holes: A full spawn list should arrive together as a formation; pressure currently sends one squad at a time.

entries.name: Plain
entries.fantasy: Open ground.
entries.rule: Cost 1.

entries.name: Road
entries.fantasy: Somebody paved this before the end of the world.
entries.rule: Cost 1.
entries.holes: Tanks should move faster on roads. Not coded.

entries.name: Rough
entries.fantasy: Rubble and broken ground.
entries.rule: Cost 2. Cost 1 for quads and flyers.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.fantasy: What is left of the suburbs.
entries.rule: Cost 2. Cost 1 for quads and flyers.
entries.holes: Designed as cover for the squad inside a skirmish. Skirmish terrain conditions are not coded.

entries.name: Water
entries.fantasy: Deep enough to drown a tank.
entries.rule: Impassable except for hover and flyer.
entries.holes: Designed to dampen burn inside a skirmish. Not coded.

entries.name: Mountain
entries.fantasy: Go around.
entries.rule: Impassable except for flyer.

entries.name: Flyer
entries.fantasy: Reaches anywhere. Holds nothing.
entries.rule: Ignores terrain cost, crosses water and mountains, cannot body-block.

entries.name: Hover
entries.fantasy: Skims the river like it is not there.
entries.rule: Crosses water.

entries.name: Quad
entries.fantasy: Four legs do not care about rubble.
entries.rule: Rough and ruins cost 1.

entries.name: Tank
entries.fantasy: Tracks and armour.
entries.rule: No effect yet.
entries.holes: Intended: faster on roads.

entries.name: City defense
entries.fantasy: The city shoots back.
entries.rule: A static player-side unit. Squads path toward it, and it joins any skirmish it is adjacent to.
entries.holes: Defenses have no die. They cannot act inside a skirmish yet.

entries.name: On attack
entries.fantasy: Whenever this mech fires.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires after the damage roll on every attack. Effects: multiply or add damage or heat, or set a minimum damage.

entries.name: On shield gain
entries.fantasy: Whenever plating goes up.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech gains shield from any source.

entries.name: On heat gain
entries.fantasy: Whenever the reactor runs hotter.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech gains heat.

entries.name: On round start
entries.fantasy: As the dice come up.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires after the roll, before rerolls.

entries.name: On skirmish start
entries.fantasy: As contact is made.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires once when the skirmish begins.

entries.name: On crit
entries.fantasy: When the round finds the seam.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires when an attack face crits. Effects: multiply or add damage, add burn to the target, vent the attacker's heat.

entries.name: On hull damage
entries.fantasy: When they get through.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires when this mech loses hull.
entries.holes: Hook for the pinned berserker idea.

entries.name: Out of combat
entries.fantasy: A phase spent not fighting.
entries.rule: Passive trigger. Fires at the end of a battlefield phase in which this mech had no skirmish.

entries.name: Command die
entries.fantasy: You are not in the machine. You are the one telling the machines what to do.
entries.rule: One die rolled alongside the mech dice each round. Faces are rechargeable commander abilities and never deal damage. Faces come from the hangar, never from rewards. Die size is a research path.
entries.holes: Open question: whether the command die exists at all, or one-shots only.

entries.name: One-shot
entries.fantasy: The button you only get to press once.
entries.rule: Consumable ability. Pouch of three. Picked up from skirmishes, expires when the battle ends. Starting stock restocks every battle.

entries.name: Reward pick
entries.fantasy: Three things on the table. Take one.
entries.rule: After a skirmish victory: a modifier on a mech face you carry, a one-shot, or a battle-wide boon. Weighted by the squad's faction.

entries.name: City ability
entries.fantasy: The city has a very large gun and a very large crane.
entries.rule: Battlefield-level ability owned and upgraded by the city: sprint, airlift, teleport, tractor beam, orbital strike. Cooldowns measured in phases.
entries.holes: Consider range limits from the gate so the push north leaves support behind.

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.fantasy: Reloading. Come back in two phases.
entries.rule: City abilities only. Counted in battlefield phases. Never used inside a skirmish.
